_doc: A294 (R5) — the key stimuli of each phase. Data only: backend/engine/key_sessions_v1.py derives the weekly key status from it at read time (never persisted). A stimulus is satisfied by a session that delivers it (families from backend/engine/stimulus.py, session_ids, technique drills, try-hard exercises, outdoor-hard days) — by DOSE, not by presence, for the anchored families. Decisions 2026-10-04 + GOAL REFRAME (technique in every phase, try-hard attached to the limit key — to the project key in performance, absent in base where there is no limit key). A294 review: outdoor days no longer count as technique (not verifiable), a limit session alone no longer counts as try-hard (a fall-practice block, outdoor near RP or a free limit session do), deload technique is info only. C272: the try-hard library drills (fall_ladder, three_attempt_comp, no_take_lead_onsight, commit_map) count for try_hard like fall_practice; they are role 'library' (composed by hand, never by the engine), so only sessions that contain them are affected. C276: two catalog sessions carry a pinned fall block — lead_tryhard_gym (falls + 2 committed routes) and route_projecting_gym (2-3 falls after the warm-up). try_hard.session_ids lets them count while still unresolved; once resolved, the fall exercise itself is checked (a session whose falls were removed does not count). A305: phase rows may declare floor_candidates / floor_target / floor_alternate — read ONLY by the planner PASS 2.7 (planner_v2._key_stimulus_pass), which places a missing key stimulus in place of a volume session; A294 (status, proposals) ignores them.

finger_max.label: Finger max
finger_max.why: Max finger strength is the strength-power phase's main adaptation: one heavy hang session a week keeps it progressing.

finger_maintenance.label: Finger maintenance
finger_maintenance.why: Power-endurance weeks keep one short max-hang session so the strength built in the previous phase is not lost.

limit_power.label: Limit / power
limit_power.why: Hard moves at your limit (limit boulders, board, campus) train recruitment and power — the stimulus that turns finger strength into climbing.

pulling_max.label: Max pulling
pulling_max.why: Heavy weighted pull-ups keep pulling strength progressing; one session a week is enough when fingers are the priority.

power_endurance.label: Power-endurance intervals
power_endurance.why: Intervals near your redpoint pace (4x4, linked boulders, route intervals) are the power-endurance phase's main adaptation.

project.label: Project
project.why: The performance phase exists to redpoint: one real projecting session a week (gym projecting, or outdoor attempts near your redpoint).

technique.label: Technique
technique.why: Feet and body positioning are your declared limiters: one weekly session of precise footwork and positioning near your limit, not easy mileage.

try_hard.label: Try-hard
try_hard.why: Falls practice and full commitment on attempts: you often stop before 100%. It rides on the limit session — it counts when that session (or another one) holds a fall-practice block (the lead try-hard session and gym projecting have one built in), or when you climb outdoors near your redpoint.
